rationale: The base station (HB-200) auto-updated to firmware 4.5, which dropped the legacy v2 radio protocol. The Living Motion sensor was still on firmware 1.1 (v2 protocol), causing E-305 "protocol v2 not supported" and a "connected_no_events" state. An OTA upgrade to firmware 1.4 (v3 protocol) was available and, once applied, restored alerts — confirming the peripheral firmware was simply outdated, not a hardware or protocol-conflict issue.

repair_steps: In the app, navigate to the Living Motion sensor's settings and trigger the OTA firmware update to version 1.4.
Wait for the update to complete (approximately 3 minutes) and confirm the sensor status changes to 'online' and alerts resume.
Advise the customer to replace the sensor battery soon, as it is at 12%.
output.customer_reply: The issue was caused by a firmware mismatch after your base station updated. I've applied an update to your Living Motion sensor, and it's now working normally. Please note the battery is low (12%), so I recommend replacing it soon to avoid future interruptions. If you need further assistance, let us know!

results.text: The peripheral firmware speaks a radio protocol the base station no longer supports, or vice versa. Frontline action: trigger OTA upgrade of the peripheral. If OTA is not available for the device or fails twice, escalate to FAE as protocol conflict.

results.source: historical_cases#H-03 Indoor camera lost after night update
results.text: After HB-200 auto-updated to 4.5, a CAM-I2 running 1.2 disconnected with E-305. OTA not offered for this hardware revision. Escalated; FAE confirmed protocol v2 dropped and arranged a compatibility firmware. Escalated correctly.

Base station firmware updates are pushed automatically at night. HB-200 firmware 4.5 removes support for the legacy v2 radio protocol. Peripherals still running v2 firmware must be upgraded to v3 firmware before or after the base station update, otherwise they disconnect.
